title: Multi-complex coexistence: rule 90 hosts two disjoint sub-complexes ({0,1} + {2,3}) simultaneously (H_295 quantitative extension)
question: Do any substrates host >=2 disjoint irreducible subsets simultaneously (multiple integration loci coexisting at the same state)?
engine: HEXAD/IIT4/lib + stdlib/consciousness/iit4_complex.complex_spectrum (returns all subsets with Phi>0, sorted). Reused, no new IIT4 code.
runtime: $0 mac-local · hexa-only · LLM none · NO GPU · deterministic (cross-process byte-identical)
finding: complex_spectrum reveals multi-complex coexistence. (1) Rule 90 hosts TWO disjoint irreducible sub-complexes simultaneously: cells {0,1} (mask=3, Phi=2) AND cells {2,3} (mask=12, Phi=2) — two independent integration loci coexisting at the same state. (2) Integrating substrates (60/110/150/105/30) host a single entry = the whole system (mask=15), no disjoint partner — the whole is the unique complex (holism). (3) Reducible substrates (constants/identity/complement) have empty spectrum. (4) Exclusion-consistent: spectrum top == find_complex (H_295). Meaning: IIT's exclusion postulate picks ONE 'the' complex, but the STRUCTURAL reality on rule 90 is multi-complex — the 4-cell ring partitions into 2 independent 2-cell integration loci (the resolution of whole-Phi=0). H_295's 'subset is the complex' becomes quantified: rule 90 has TWO such subsets, equal Phi, disjoint. The ECA parity-ring's even-cell/odd-cell bipartite structure is the substrate of that partition.
honest_limits: L1: complex_spectrum is state-dependent (state 5 single point); multi-disjoint classification may shift at other states.
L2: n=4 small (only 2-cell sub-partitions visible); large-n multi-complex partition patterns explode super-exponentially.
L3: multi-complex (subset-irreducibility) differs from PID redundancy (information-flow decomposition).
L4: IIT exclusion picks one; multi-spectrum is STRUCTURAL candidate-set, not a phenomenal multi-consciousness claim.
L5: ECA proxy; not a phenomenal claim.
L6: structure-cut big-Phi; relative comparison robust.
L7: verdict is a toy-substrate measurement fact.
